\section{The exact conditional oracle and uniform construction}

Apply (12) to each of the original $2^c$ frequency matrices in (5), keep its
original affine phase, and divide by $2^c$. This is the conditional count.
The code checks integrality and nonnegativity. When the next row becomes
complete, it is moved to $P$ and the same rule is reused. At a fully fixed
$Y$, the count is zero if (2) fails or $\row Z\nsubseteq\row Y$; otherwise
it is exactly
\[
 q^{p(d-\rank Y)},                                           \tag{13}
\]
the size of the affine solution set for $X$.

Start at $N>0$. At each binary coordinate of $Y$, compute the zero-child
count $N_0$. The one-child count is $N-N_0$. For a uniform sample choose
zero with probability $N_0/N$, using an exact uniform integer in
$\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. For a witness, take the zero child whenever $N_0>0$ and
otherwise the one child. Update the current count and continue.
There are $adr$ bit decisions. After the complete $Y$ is chosen, solve
each left-row system $xY=z$. For sampling, choose a uniformly random
element of its affine kernel translate; for search, choose a particular
solution. Each field coordinate is an $a$-bit uniform word, so there is
no enumeration of the field.

For a complete $Y$ with $M_Y$ left completions, the prefix probabilities
telescope to $M_Y/N$. Conditional left sampling chooses each completion
with probability $1/M_Y$. Every pair $(X,Y)$ therefore has probability
$1/N$. This proof uses the final positive conditional counts; individual
signed character coefficients are never treated as probabilities.
Integer interval draws can use rejection of bit strings with acceptance
at least one half. This is unrelated to rejection from a rare constrained
matrix-product fiber.

\section{Actual coordinate manufacture and original-input reconstruction}

The code reuses the proved constructive procedure
\path|ManufacturedMatrixCoordinates| from
\path|acquired_rank_one_slice_sampler.py|. This coordinate constructor
itself does not require the rank-one-dual hypothesis.
It acquires the center field from its actual multiplication table, splits
primitive corners by random elements and the binary-linear idempotent
equation in a generated commutative algebra, then constructs connecting
matrix units by linear equations. The inherited corner lemma gives success
probability at least $1/(8h)$ in a corner $M_h(\F_q)

source_excerpts.text:
\section{Affine slice, exact sampling, and cost}

The original affine slice contributes its original $2^c$ independent
characters and their phases. Apply the preceding formula to each one and
divide by $2^c$. The number of characters does not increase with the prefix
length. At a completely fixed $Y$, the result is zero unless its affine
constraints hold and $\row Z\subseteq\row Y$; otherwise it is
$q^{p(d-\rank Y)}$. This agrees with solving the left linear fibers.

Successively choose right-matrix bits with probability equal to their exact
completion count divided by the parent count. Once $Y$ is complete, solve
each left-row affine system and draw uniformly from its kernel translate.
The prefix probabilities telescope: a right matrix is selected with its
number of left completions divided by the full population, and each
completion is then selected with the reciprocal of that number. Every
original matrix pair therefore has exactly equal probability. The acquired
coordinate maps and corrected original affine reconstruction are bijective,
so uniformity carries back to the original independent inputs.

There are at most $adr$ bit-prefix decisions. Each query uses $2^c$
characters, three polynomial-size binary solves per character, and the
polynomial signed-fiber scalar. Finite-field arithmetic is manufactured,
not an oracle; all integers have polynomial bit length. The bound is
$2^c\operatorname{poly}(a,p,d,r)$ per sample after coordinate acquisition.
The native gate frontend enforces $2^c$ no larger than the actual compact
input-description byte length, giving a polynomially admitted native family.
For unrestricted $c$, the explicit exponential dependence remains.
Random integer interval draws and inherited coordinate acquisition have
polynomial expectation; no universal worst-case random-bit bound is claimed.

source_excerpts.text:
## A. Positive sampling requires a proved conditional family

The acquired form is (h0+iota(v))(u)=y, with the complete original affine
bijection retained. X has p by d entries and Y has d by r entries over
F_(2^a); the right slice is binary affine of codimension c, not necessarily
linear over the extension field. The signed universal product fiber has an
explicit finite Gaussian double sum. The inherited independent derivation
instead applies row-space Mobius inversion; neither is an assumed oracle.
The reverse Hom pairing uses a nonzero functional annihilating commutators,
not the represented binary trace which may vanish at even multiplicity.

If t complete rows span A of rank alpha, quotient by A. The remaining
frequency rows must annihilate A. The free block and X-extension count is
q^[alpha(d-t)+p(t-alpha)]. Appending the next frequency row changes the two
relevant ranks in only three ways: (ell,rho), (ell+1,rho), (ell+1,rho+1).
Their domains are nested binary-linear preimages K contained in L contained
in E. The summand is (f0-f1)1_K+(f1-f2)1_L+f2 1_E. Each signed affine mass is
zero or a signed power of two, obtained by elimination. Consequently only
the original 2^c characters are summed, with no exponential prefix factor.

After the Fourier sum, integer nonnegative completion counts, not signed
terms, select the next bit. Branch ratios telescope to a uniform Y weighted
by its X fiber; an independent uniform affine solve for X gives the uniform
factor pair and then the original input. This proves acquired-row-prefix
sampling, not closure under arbitrary original-input pins. The native wrapper
checks 2^c against actual compact-description BYTES before preprocessing;
unrestricted c is still exponential. Exact unbiased integer draws have an
expected-time contract; optional seeded PRNG runs do not prove hardware or
information-theoretic randomness. The loose native expected O(L^29) bound is
not practical speed or bounded worst-case random-bit use.
